title: Restaurant and Retail Waste
description: One-minute skill: Restaurant and Retail Waste.

hook.text: An average US restaurant wastes 25,000–75,000 pounds of food per year. Buffets are the worst offenders.

buildup.text: Oversized portions, unpredictable demand, and strict health regulations all contribute to commercial food waste.

discovery.text: Apps like Too Good To Go sell surplus restaurant and bakery food at a discount, reaching 80 million users.

twist.text: Good Samaritan laws protect food donors from liability—yet most businesses don't know these protections exist.

climax.text: France banned supermarkets from throwing away edible food in 2016—requiring donation to food banks instead.

punchline.text: One country's law turned trash into meals. The food was always fine—just unsold.

quiz.question: What did France do about supermarket food waste in 2016?
options: Banned disposal of edible food, requiring donation to food banks

details.summary: Restaurants and retailers generate enormous food waste through overproduction, strict appearance standards, buffet leftovers, and unsold inventory. This topic examines the scale, causes, and growing movement to reduce commercial food waste.
details.whyItMatters: Restaurants and stores waste food worth billions annually while millions go hungry. Reducing commercial waste is a win-win for business profitability and social responsibility.
takeaways: Restaurants waste an estimated 15–25% of the food they purchase
Supermarkets reject produce that fails cosmetic standards despite being nutritious
Apps like Too Good To Go connect consumers with surplus restaurant food at low cost

faq.question: Why do restaurants waste so much food?
faq.answer: Restaurants must maintain diverse menus and handle unpredictable demand, leading to over-preparation. Buffets, large portions, plate waste, spoilage from over-ordering, and rigid food safety policies all contribute to high waste rates.

faq.question: How are retailers reducing food waste?
faq.answer: Retailers are selling 'ugly' produce at discount, donating unsold food to charities, using dynamic pricing based on expiration dates, improving demand forecasting with AI, and partnering with surplus food apps for end-of-day redistribution.
